Metadata.title: Manic Accounting: Manic about your numbers. Calm about your books.
Metadata.description: Bookkeeping, month-end close, budgets, 13-week cash flow and VAT preparation for small businesses and freelancers.

Metadata.contactDescription: Tell me what keeps you up at night. Replies within two working days.

Home.intro: Hi, I’m Manic. I’ve spent a decade inside the finance teams of big multinationals. Now I take on a handful of smaller businesses who want clean books, filed taxes and a cash flow they can see coming.
Home.trustOne: A decade in finance and controlling
Home.trustTwo: VAT and tax filing across Czechia, Bulgaria and Romania
Home.trustThree: Month-end close for EU, US and Canadian entities
Home.toolTitle: How much debt can the business safely repay?
Home.toolIntro: This 13-week view connects debt repayments to the thing that matters: cash left after running the business. Adjust the plan, protect a minimum buffer and stress-test what happens when sales slip or costs rise.

Services.title: The boring stuff, done properly.
Services.intro: Month-end, tax deadlines, reconciliations, forecasts. The things that never feel urgent until they very much are.

Process.title: No jargon. No surprises. Slightly obsessive.
Process.stepOneText: Thirty minutes, free. You tell me what hurts. I tell you honestly whether I can help.
Process.stepTwoText: I go through what you have and tell you what is off, in plain language, with a fix for each point.
Process.stepThreeText: A monthly close, a reporting calendar and tax deadlines locked in. You always know what happens when.
Process.stepFourText: Numbers arrive on time and make sense. I carry on being a little bit manic so you do not have to be.

About.title: Yes, Manic is my real surname.
About.paragraphOne: Everybody makes the joke, so I made it the brand. Behind the pun is a decade in finance and controlling: from general ledger and reconciliations to leading a finance team and steering costs across global functions of a multinational.
About.paragraphTwo: I have closed the books for entities in Europe, the US and Canada, built process automation for accounting teams, and filed VAT in three countries. By day I am a finance controller. Now I am bringing the same obsessiveness to a few smaller businesses who deserve it too.

Workflow.overline: FROM SOURCE DATA TO USEFUL ANSWERS
Workflow.title: Messy inputs in. Clear decisions out.
Workflow.intro: The real work sits between receiving the files and delivering the answer: checking, matching, reconciling and explaining what changed.
Workflow.caption: Not magic. A repeatable process, with every number traceable back to its source.

scenarioNote.base: The current plan, using the weekly inflows and operating costs below.
scenarioNote.salesDip: Customer receipts are reduced by 15%. A useful check before promising a repayment schedule.
scenarioNote.costRise: Operating costs are increased by 10% to show how quickly repayment headroom can narrow.

verdict.healthy: The plan keeps the cash buffer intact. Planned repayment is {planned} per week; the estimated safe ceiling is {safe}.
verdict.tight: Cash stays above zero, but the buffer is missed by {amount} in week {week}. Reduce or reschedule repayments before the plan becomes fragile.
verdict.shortfall: The plan runs short of cash. The lowest point misses the buffer by {amount} in week {week}. The debt schedule needs to change before it is committed.

CashFlow.disclaimer: This is a planning illustration, not a lending decision. A real review also checks repayment terms, interest, tax timing, seasonality and the reliability of customer collections.
